current_row.boundary_rationale: A fresh word-event formula opens the unit, וַיְהִי֙ דְּבַר יְהוָ֔ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.32.26, byte), matching “Then Yahweh’s word came to Jeremiah, saying,” (web:Jer.32.26), turning address from Jeremiah’s own prayer to Yahweh’s own reply. That reply opens on a rhetorical question answering the prayer’s own premise, הִנֵּה֙ אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֔ה אֱלֹהֵ֖י כָּל בָּשָׂ֑ר הֲֽמִמֶּ֔נִּי יִפָּלֵ֖א כָּל דָּבָֽר (oshb:Jer.32.27, byte), matching “Behold, I am Yahweh, the God of all flesh. Is there anything too hard for me?” (web:Jer.32.27), and a judgment sentence follows at once, לָכֵ֕ן כֹּ֖ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.32.28, byte), matching “Therefore Yahweh says: Behold, I will give this city into the hand of the Chaldeans, and into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon” (web:Jer.32.28), naming the king in the same resh-family spelling read at the chapter’s own opening. The reasons for the judgment follow without any new speaker or addressee — rooftop incense and drink offerings to Baal and other gods (web:Jer.32.29), Israel and Judah’s evil from their youth (web:Jer.32.30), the city’s own long provocation (web:Jer.32.31), and every rank of the guilty named in turn, “they, their kings, their princes, their priests, their prophets, the men of Judah, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem” (web:Jer.32.32) — closing on the high places built for Baal in the valley of the son of Hinnom, to make their children pass through the fire to Molech, וַיִּבְנוּ֩ אֶת בָּמ֨וֹת הַבַּ֜עַל אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּגֵ֣יא בֶן הִנֹּ֗ם לְ֠הַעֲבִיר אֶת בְּנֵיהֶ֣ם וְאֶת בְּנוֹתֵיהֶם֮ לַמֹּלֶךְ֒ (oshb:Jer.32.35, byte tier), matching “They built the high places of Baal, which are in the valley of the son of Hinnom, to cause their sons and their daughters to pass through fire to Molech” (web:Jer.32.35). The whole indictment is held as one continuous reply because nothing inside it reopens address to a new party; the turn comes only at a compound turn phrase, וְעַתָּ֕ה לָכֵ֛ן (oshb:Jer.32.36, byte), matching “Now therefore” (web:Jer.32.36), that reopens the reply toward this city’s own restoration, and this row stops just short of that turn. At oshb:Jer.32.35 (WLC, single-witness), this verse's own close carries a ketiv/qere pair on the verb of causing-to-sin, החטי הַחֲטִ֥יא, standing clear of the slice above, which is verse-initial while the note sits at the verse's own end.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Holding the whole divine reply from verse 26 through the end of the chapter as one unbroken row was considered, since no frame-owner change interrupts it anywhere; it is rejected because the second-person plural pronoun אַתֶּ֣ם (oshb:Jer.32.36, byte tier) makes its first appearance in the reply at that verse, marking an explicit third-to-second person addressee shift after ten verses carrying none, a tier-1 class this campaign treats as a legitimate internal cut even without a change of speaker.
current_row.literature_type_guess: the judgment half of Yahweh’s own answer to the prayer

current_row.boundary_rationale: A compound turn particle reopens address toward the city itself, וְעַתָּ֕ה לָכֵ֛ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אֶל הָעִ֨יר הַזֹּ֜את אֲשֶׁ֣ר אַתֶּ֣ם אֹמְרִ֗ים (oshb:Jer.32.36, byte), matching “Now therefore Yahweh, the God of Israel, says concerning this city, about which you say,” (web:Jer.32.36), quoting back the current public verdict, “It is given into the hand of the king of Babylon by the sword, by the famine, and by the pestilence” (web:Jer.32.36). The promise that answers it follows without a break, “Behold, I will gather them out of all the countries where I have driven them” (web:Jer.32.37), through an everlasting covenant, “I will make an everlasting covenant with them, that I will not turn away from following them, to do them good” (web:Jer.32.40), and joy over their own good, “I will rejoice over them to do them good, and I will plant them in this land assuredly with my whole heart and with my whole soul” (web:Jer.32.41). A further formula, כִּֽי כֹה֙ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.32.42, byte), matching “For Yahweh says:” (web:Jer.32.42), carries the same reply forward rather than opening a new one, since no addressee or frame-owner change accompanies it; it bridges directly into the same quoted-objection construction read at this row’s own opening, אֲשֶׁ֣ר אַתֶּ֣ם אֹמְרִ֗ים (oshb:Jer.32.43, byte), matching “Fields will be bought in this land, about which you say,” (web:Jer.32.43), before quoting the same desolate-land verdict in different words, closing the whole chapter on the same field-purchase vocabulary that opened it, כִּֽי אָשִׁ֥יב אֶת שְׁבוּתָ֖ם (oshb:Jer.32.44, byte), matching “for I will cause their captivity to be reversed,” (web:Jer.32.44) “says Yahweh” (web:Jer.32.44). Nothing between verse 36 and this row's own close reopens a frame-owner or addressee shift, so the restoration promise and its own field-purchase close are held as one unit; the row is bounded by the fresh word-event formula that opens the next unit, וַיְהִ֧י דְבַר יְהוָ֛ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ שֵׁנִ֑ית (oshb:Jer.33.1, byte tier), matching “Moreover Yahweh’s word came to Jeremiah the second time,” (web:Jer.33.1).
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting a fresh row at verse 42, where the reply opens with a further messenger formula, or at verse 43, where the field-purchase vocabulary itself returns, was considered; both are rejected on the same ground applied at this row’s own opening — neither carries a frame-owner or addressee change of its own, and the whole span from verse 36 reads as one sustained promise closing the chapter on the sign it began with.
current_row.literature_type_guess: the restoration promise closing the field-purchase sign

A petuchah closes the span and the chapter at oshb:Jer.32.44. The three-word construction אֲשֶׁ֣ר אַתֶּ֣ם אֹמְרִ֗ים (oshb:Jer.32.36, byte tier), rendered “about which you say” (web:Jer.32.36), is byte-identical at oshb:Jer.32.43 (sweep: 2 verses, byte tier, MT keys); the third site, oshb:Jer.33.10, carries an added meteg that survives the accent strip and matches only at the consonantal-skeleton tier, where the construction stands in exactly 3 verses and nowhere else in the book (sweep: 3 verses, skeleton tier, MT keys, at oshb:Jer.32.36, oshb:Jer.32.43 and oshb:Jer.33.10). The closing captivity-reversal formula אָשִׁ֥יב אֶת שְׁבוּתָ֖ם (oshb:Jer.32.44, byte) recurs in this exact inflected form in the book only at oshb:Jer.33.26 (sweep: 2 verses), closing this row on language its own later echo will repeat, disclosed here as cross-seam cohesion rather than as evidence for either boundary.

current_row.boundary_rationale: A fresh koh-amar onset reopens the quoted-objection construction read twice already at oshb:Jer.32.36 and oshb:Jer.32.43, כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה עוֹד֮ יִשָּׁמַ֣ע בַּמָּקוֹם הַזֶּה֒ אֲשֶׁר֙ אַתֶּ֣ם (oshb:Jer.33.10, byte), matching “Yahweh says:” (web:Jer.33.10), “Yet again there will be heard in this place, about which you say,” (web:Jer.33.10), answering the despairing report, “It is waste, without man and without animal” (web:Jer.33.10), with a promise of sound returning, “the voice of joy and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride” (web:Jer.33.11). A second promise follows, opened by its own fresh formula and an expanded divine title, כֹּֽה אָמַר֮ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָאוֹת֒ ע֞וֹד יִֽהְיֶ֣ה בַּמָּק֣וֹם הַזֶּ֗ה (oshb:Jer.33.12, byte), matching “Yahweh of Armies says:” (web:Jer.33.12), “Yet again there will be in this place, which is waste, without man and without animal” (web:Jer.33.12), now of shepherds and flocks rather than wedding sounds, closing on עֹ֣ד תַּעֲבֹ֧רְנָה הַצֹּ֛אן עַל יְדֵ֥י מוֹנֶ֖ה אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה (oshb:Jer.33.13, byte tier), matching “the flocks will again pass under the hands of him who counts them,” “says Yahweh” (web:Jer.33.13). The two promises are held as one unit: both open on the same yet-again adverb over the same ruined place, neither introduces a new addressee, and nothing marks a frame-owner change between the sound of joy and the sound of flocks. The next span opens on a differently shaped formula altogether, “Behold, the days come,” (web:Jer.33.14), and this row stops before it.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the wedding-sound promise of verses 10 and 11 from the shepherd-and-flock promise of verses 12 and 13 into two rows was considered, since each opens its own koh-amar formula; it is rejected because neither formula carries an addressee or frame-owner change, and both promises share the same yet-again opening adverb over the same devastated place, read here as one twinned promise rather than two independent oracles.
current_row.literature_type_guess: the twinned promise of returning sound and returning flocks
current_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate

A paseq falls inside this span at oshb:Jer.33.10 and again at oshb:Jer.33.12 (WLC, single-witness, seg layer, count-only, no intra-verse position claimed). The three-word construction אֲשֶׁר֙ אַתֶּ֣ם אֹֽמְרִ֔ים (oshb:Jer.33.10, byte tier), matching “about which you say” (web:Jer.33.10), is the third and last book-wide site of the construction read earlier at oshb:Jer.32.36 and oshb:Jer.32.43, at the consonantal-skeleton tier (sweep: 3 verses, skeleton tier, MT keys); the two earlier sites are byte-identical with each other (sweep: 2 verses, byte tier, MT keys) but carry distinct pointing from this verse, matching this verse's own pointing at the weaker, skeleton tier alone.

current_row.boundary_rationale: A differently shaped formula opens the unit, הִנֵּ֛ה יָמִ֥ים בָּאִ֖ים נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.33.14, byte), matching “Behold, the days come,” says Yahweh, “that I will perform that good word” (web:Jer.33.14), naming its own object, “concerning the house of Israel and concerning the house of Judah” (web:Jer.33.14). A dynastic promise follows at once, אַצְמִ֥יחַ לְדָוִ֖ד צֶ֣מַח צְדָקָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.33.15, byte), matching “I will cause a Branch of righteousness to grow up to David” (web:Jer.33.15), naming the city’s own new title, לָ֖הּ יְהוָ֥ה צִדְקֵֽנוּ (oshb:Jer.33.16, byte), matching “Yahweh our righteousness” (web:Jer.33.16). The promise continues without any addressee shift into the Davidic throne guarantee, introduced by a ki-subordinated koh-amar formula, כִּי כֹ֖ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.33.17, byte tier), matching “For Yahweh says:” (web:Jer.33.17), “David will never lack a man to sit on the throne of the house of Israel” (web:Jer.33.17), and turning to the parallel guarantee for the priesthood on a plain waw with no speech formula of its own, וְלַכֹּהֲנִים֙ הַלְוִיִּ֔ם (oshb:Jer.33.18, byte tier), matching “The Levitical priests won’t lack a man before me to offer burnt offerings” (web:Jer.33.18). The turn from throne to altar falls at verse 18, not at the koh-amar of verse 17, which itself carries no addressee or frame-owner change and only introduces the throne guarantee; the Branch prophecy and the double dynastic-priestly guarantee are held as one unit because nothing between them reopens address to a new party. A fresh word-event formula turns the unit again, “Yahweh’s word came to Jeremiah, saying,” (web:Jer.33.19), and this row ends just before it.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting a fresh row at verse 18, where the guarantee turns from David's throne to the Levitical altar on a plain waw with no speech formula of its own, was considered; it is rejected because that turn carries no addressee or frame-owner change, extending the same dynastic guarantee to a second office rather than opening an unrelated promise.
current_row.literature_type_guess: the Davidic Branch and the dynastic-priestly guarantee

current_row.device_notes: A setumah marks the span immediately before its own opening at oshb:Jer.33.13, a further setumah falls inside the span at oshb:Jer.33.16, and a third closes the span at oshb:Jer.33.18 (single-witness WLC evidence; weak, tier-3 corroboration under the Prophets addendum). A paseq falls inside the span at oshb:Jer.33.16 (WLC, single-witness, seg layer, count-only). The two guarantees share a repeated verb, לֹֽא יִכָּרֵ֣ת (oshb:Jer.33.17, byte) and לֹֽא יִכָּרֵ֥ת (oshb:Jer.33.18, byte), both matching “will never lack” / “won’t lack” (web:Jer.33.17, web:Jer.33.18), disclosed here as the verbal thread binding the two verses into one guarantee rather than two. current_row.boundary_rationale: A fresh word-event formula opens the unit on its own, וַֽיְהִי֙ דְּבַר יְהוָ֔ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ לֵאמֽוֹר (oshb:Jer.33.19, byte), matching “Yahweh’s word came to Jeremiah, saying,” (web:Jer.33.19), the third such formula after oshb:Jer.32.26 and oshb:Jer.33.1. The reply that follows opens on a conditional analogy, כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה אִם תָּפֵ֨רוּ֙ אֶת בְּרִיתִ֣י הַיּ֔וֹם וְאֶת בְּרִיתִ֖י הַלָּ֑יְלָה (oshb:Jer.33.20, byte tier), matching “Yahweh says: ‘If you can break my covenant of the day and my covenant of the night” (web:Jer.33.20), extending it at once to David's own line, matching “then my covenant could also be broken with David my servant, that he won’t have a son to reign on his throne” (web:Jer.33.21), “and with the Levitical priests, my ministers” (web:Jer.33.21). It closes on a second analogy, drawn from the uncountable host of heaven and the immeasurable sand of the sea rather than from the day-night covenant itself, אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא יִסָּפֵר֙ צְבָ֣א הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וְלֹ֥א יִמַּ֖ד ח֣וֹל הַיָּ֑ם כֵּ֣ן אַרְבֶּ֗ה אֶת זֶ֨רַע֙ דָּוִ֣ד עַבְדִּ֔י וְאֶת הַלְוִיִּ֖ם מְשָׁרְתֵ֥י אֹתִֽי (oshb:Jer.33.22, byte tier), matching “As the army of the sky can’t be counted, and the sand of the sea can’t be measured, so I will multiply the offspring of David my servant and the Levites who minister to me” (web:Jer.33.22). No addressee or frame-owner change interrupts this span between the day-night analogy and its own application to David and the Levites; a further fresh word-event formula reopens address again immediately after, “Yahweh’s word came to Jeremiah, saying,” (web:Jer.33.23), and this row is bounded there.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding this row into the Davidic Branch promise that precedes it, reading verses 14 through 22 as one continuous consolation, was considered; it is rejected because a fresh word-event formula reopens address at verse 19, the same tier-1 device read at oshb:Jer.32.26 and oshb:Jer.33.1, treated as a primary macro-seam wherever it recurs.
current_row.literature_type_guess: the day-night covenant analogy guaranteeing David and the Levites

current_row.boundary_rationale: The unit opens on the prose-sermon header, הַדָּבָ֛ר אֲשֶׁר הָיָ֥ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ מֵאֵ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.34.1, byte), matching “The word which came to Jeremiah from Yahweh,” (web:Jer.34.1) -- the siege itself named in the same breath, וּנְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֣ר מֶֽלֶךְ בָּבֶ֣ל וְכָל חֵיל֡וֹ וְכָל מַמְלְכ֣וֹת אֶרֶץ֩ מֶמְשֶׁ֨לֶת יָד֜וֹ וְכָל הָעַמִּ֗ים נִלְחָמִ֧ים עַל יְרוּשָׁלִַ֛ם וְעַל כָּל עָרֶ֖יהָ לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.34.1, byte), matching “when Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, with all his army, all the kingdoms of the earth that were under his dominion, and all the peoples, were fighting against Jerusalem and against all its cities, saying:” (web:Jer.34.1) A single envoy commission follows without a break: כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הָלֹךְ֙ וְאָ֣מַרְתָּ֔ אֶל צִדְקִיָּ֖הוּ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֵלָ֗יו (oshb:Jer.34.2, byte), matching “Yahweh, the God of Israel, says, 'Go, and speak to Zedekiah king of Judah, and tell him,” (web:Jer.34.2) -- Yahweh's word for Zedekiah's city. A second, contrasting word for Zedekiah's own person opens on the same address rather than a new one, אַ֚ךְ שְׁמַ֣ע דְּבַר יְהוָ֔ה צִדְקִיָּ֖הוּ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.34.4, byte), matching “Yet hear Yahweh's word, O Zedekiah king of Judah.” (web:Jer.34.4) promising the king he will die in peace and be mourned with the funeral cry וְה֥וֹי אָד֖וֹן יִסְפְּדוּ לָ֑ךְ (oshb:Jer.34.5, byte) -- the vav-prefixed ve-hoy shape only, a funeral acclamation for the king rather than a woe-oracle onset, matching “They will lament you, saying, "Ah Lord!” (web:Jer.34.5) Jeremiah's own delivery of the whole message closes the scene, וַיְדַבֵּר֙ יִרְמְיָ֣הוּ הַנָּבִ֔יא אֶל צִדְקִיָּ֖הוּ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.34.6, byte), matching “Then Jeremiah the prophet spoke all these words to Zedekiah king of Judah in Jerusalem,” (web:Jer.34.6) and the row ends on the siege notice that answers the opening one, וְחֵ֣יל מֶֽלֶךְ בָּבֶ֗ל נִלְחָמִים֙ עַל יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם (oshb:Jer.34.7, byte), matching “when the king of Babylon's army was fighting against Jerusalem” (web:Jer.34.7) naming Lachish and Azekah as the last fortified cities still holding. A fresh prose-sermon header opens at הַדָּבָ֛ר אֲשֶׁר הָיָ֥ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ מֵאֵ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.34.8, byte), matching “The word came to Jeremiah from Yahweh,” (web:Jer.34.8) and this row does not reach past that turn.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting a fresh row at the contrastive turn opening verse 4 was rejected because the addressee stays Zedekiah throughout and no koh-amar frame-owner change or new envoy scene marks that inner pivot -- it remains the single message Jeremiah is sent to deliver.

The hoy at Jer.34.5 is named here as the vav-prefixed funeral-cry shape specifically, distinct in role from the book's woe onsets, day-alas cry, and sword apostrophe, none of which this row engages.

current_row.boundary_rationale: A second prose-sermon header opens its own unit, הַדָּבָ֛ר אֲשֶׁר הָיָ֥ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ מֵאֵ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.34.8, byte), matching “The word came to Jeremiah from Yahweh,” (web:Jer.34.8) dated after אַחֲרֵ֡י כְּרֹת֩ הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ צִדְקִיָּ֜הוּ בְּרִ֗ית (oshb:Jer.34.8, byte), matching “after King Zedekiah had made a covenant” (web:Jer.34.8) -- a covenant to free every Hebrew bondservant, לְ֠שַׁלַּח אִ֣ישׁ אֶת עַבְדּ֞וֹ וְאִ֧ישׁ אֶת שִׁפְחָת֛וֹ הָעִבְרִ֥י וְהָעִבְרִיָּ֖ה חָפְשִׁ֑ים (oshb:Jer.34.9, byte), matching “that every man should let his male servant, and every man his female servant, who is a Hebrew or a Hebrewess, go free,” (web:Jer.34.9) The princes and people comply and the servants go free (web:Jer.34.10), but the row closes on the reversal, the full verse וַיָּשׁ֨וּבוּ֙ אַחֲרֵי כֵ֔ן וַיָּשִׁ֗בוּ אֶת הָֽעֲבָדִים֙ וְאֶת הַשְּׁפָח֔וֹת אֲשֶׁ֥ר שִׁלְּח֖וּ חָפְשִׁ֑ים ויכבישום וַֽיִּכְבְּשׁ֔וּם לַעֲבָדִ֖ים וְלִשְׁפָחֽוֹת (oshb:Jer.34.11, byte), matching “but afterwards they turned, and caused the servants and the handmaids whom they had let go free to return, and brought them into subjection for servants and for handmaids.” (web:Jer.34.11) -- a ketiv/qere pair sits inside this same clause, the unpointed ketiv ויכבישום immediately followed by the pointed qere וַֽיִּכְבְּשׁ֔וּם ((oshb:Jer.34.11, byte), single-witness WLC), both read here rather than silently reduced to one form. A fresh word-event formula opens Yahweh's own reply at וַיְהִ֤י דְבַר יְהוָה֙ אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ מֵאֵ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.34.12, byte), matching “Therefore Yahweh's word came to Jeremiah from Yahweh, saying,” (web:Jer.34.12) and this row stops at the narrated reversal, short of that reply.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding this narrated covenant and its collapse together with Yahweh's response beginning at verse 12 into one continuous unit was considered, since both concern the same episode, but rejected because verse 12 carries its own fresh word-event formula, a tier-1 onset the campaign treats as its own row boundary regardless of topical continuity.

current_row.boundary_rationale: Yahweh's own word-event formula opens the reply, the full verse וַיְהִ֤י דְבַר יְהוָה֙ אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ מֵאֵ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.34.12, byte), matching “Therefore Yahweh's word came to Jeremiah from Yahweh, saying,” (web:Jer.34.12) A koh-amar recitation of the ancient release law follows, כֹּֽה אָמַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אָנֹכִ֗י כָּרַ֤תִּֽי בְרִית֙ אֶת אֲב֣וֹתֵיכֶ֔ם (oshb:Jer.34.13, byte), matching “Yahweh, the God of Israel, says: 'I made a covenant with your fathers” (web:Jer.34.13) tracing the fathers' original disobedience and this generation's own recent turning and reversal (web:Jer.34.14-Jer.34.16). A setumah (single-witness WLC; weak, tier-3 corroboration under the Prophets addendum) falls at oshb:Jer.34.16, exactly at the pivot from that recitation to the sentence pronounced next. The sentence itself opens without a change of speaker or addressee, לָכֵן֮ כֹּה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָה֒ אַתֶּם֙ לֹֽא שְׁמַעְתֶּ֣ם אֵלַ֔י לִקְרֹ֣א דְר֔וֹר אִ֥ישׁ לְאָחִ֖יו וְאִ֣ישׁ לְרֵעֵ֑הוּ (oshb:Jer.34.17, byte), matching “Therefore Yahweh says: "You have not listened to me, to proclaim liberty, every man to his brother,” (web:Jer.34.17) continuing into the ironic proclamation of a 'liberty' to calamity, הִנְנִ֣י קֹרֵא֩ לָכֶ֨ם דְּר֜וֹר נְאֻם יְהוָ֗ה אֶל הַחֶ֨רֶב֙ אֶל הַדֶּ֣בֶר וְאֶל הָרָעָ֔ב וְנָתַתִּ֤י אֶתְכֶם֙ (oshb:Jer.34.17, byte), matching “Behold, I proclaim to you a liberty," says Yahweh, "to the sword, to the pestilence, and to the famine.” (web:Jer.34.17) -- a ketiv/qere pair sits at the close of this same clause, the unpointed ketiv לזועה immediately followed by the pointed qere לְזַעֲוָ֔ה ((oshb:Jer.34.17, byte), single-witness WLC). The covenant-breakers are named through the ritual they violated, הָעֵ֨גֶל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר כָּרְת֣וּ לִשְׁנַ֔יִם וַיַּעַבְר֖וּ בֵּ֥ין בְּתָרָֽיו (oshb:Jer.34.18, byte), matching “cut the calf in two and passed between its parts:” (web:Jer.34.18) and the row closes on the command to renew the siege, הִנְנִ֨י מְצַוֶּ֜ה נְאֻם יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Jer.34.22, byte), matching “Behold, I will command," says Yahweh,” (web:Jer.34.22) A petuchah (single-witness WLC; weak, tier-3 corroboration under the Prophets addendum) closes this same verse. A fresh prose-sermon header, dated instead to the days of Jehoiakim, opens the next unit at הַדָּבָ֛ר אֲשֶׁר הָיָ֥ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ מֵאֵ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.35.1, byte), matching “The word which came to Jeremiah from Yahweh” (web:Jer.35.1) and this row does not reach past the sentence pronounced here.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting a fresh row at the therefore-clause opening verse 17, where recitation turns to formal sentence, was considered, but rejected because the campaign ties a koh-amar-driven cut to a change of whose mouth carries the formula, and the same divine speaker addresses the same covenant-breakers on both sides of that turn.
